title: MinuteProof: red flags from board minutes, with proof
audience: Judges and attendees of a one-hour Reducto hackathon, including viewers new to board minutes, due diligence, Reducto and DuckDB.
outcome: The viewer understands that hundreds of pages of board minutes became a cited red-flag report in minutes: they can find the result, a recurring problem and its trail, and open the original page behind a flag.
tone: Conversational and plain, second person, every term defined the first time; vision only over the outro card, worded as vision.

participants.agent: a separate reviewer session arranged by the team lead

sources.description: Snapshot of /api/due-diligence/summary the page renders (equal to the live API on 2026-11-04): pages read, red flags, deferred or unresolved, reading time saved, extraction minutes and jobs. Authoritative for those totals as computed by the pipeline; not an independent audit of the minutes.

Snapshot of /api/due-diligence/recurring: recurring issues with meetings, flagged mentions, first/last dates and the latest status and summary. Authoritative for what the page shows about recurring issues; derived from the Reducto extracts by DuckDB.

Snapshot of /api/due-diligence/red-flags: every flagged item with date, category, reason, quote and cited page. Authoritative for what each flag says and which page it cites; the reasons are model-written summaries of the quoted paragraph.
Snapshot of /api/due-diligence/spend: approved spend by quarter and category, the source of the spend chart. Silent on anything beyond quarterly totals.
The Vaucluse House trust minute book 1972-73 (298 pages), the primary source; page 7 holds the 20 Feb 1972 wharf paragraph the first flag quotes.
The Vaucluse House trust minute book 1974-75 (420 pages), the primary source for the latest wharf entry (page 273, 16 Mar 1975, the pile stump).

The team's build contract: how Reducto Extract output (with citations and absolute PDF pages) is flattened into items and grouped with DuckDB. Authoritative for how the pipeline is meant to work; it is a plan written by the team, not a measurement.

claims.quote: seven hundred eighteen pages of minutes became one hundred twenty-eight red flags
one hundred thirty-four items were put off or left unresolved
you skip about twenty-four hours of reading

The latest, in March nineteen seventy-five, is a dangerous old pile stump. It's still deferred
Its first flag is from February nineteen seventy-two.
The board warned the wharf was getting worse, and two agencies couldn't agree who should maintain it.
Below is the exact text, with its citation: the page it came from.
One click opens that page, so you can check it yourself.
White ants, which are termites, come up at six meetings.

These buttons filter the flags by type.
This chart follows the money, three months per bar.
One: Reducto reads every page. Two: it pulls out each decision, repair, dollar amount and dispute, and notes its page.
Three: DuckDB groups them over time, to find what keeps coming back. Four: every claim links to its page.
Here, the reading took about six minutes.
Hundreds of pages of board minutes became a cited red-flag report in minutes.
